title: Fei-Fei Li on Spatial Intelligence and Robotics

reader_summary.headline: Fei-Fei Li explains how spatial intelligence and digital worlds will advance robotics.
reader_summary.overview: Fei-Fei Li describes spatial intelligence as the next step for AI, allowing it to understand both physical and virtual spaces. She explains how digital simulations let robots learn safely and quickly by practicing in consistent worlds that match reality. This approach helps robots master complex tasks before working in messy real environments.

key_points.text: Spatial intelligence lets AI understand and act in both physical and virtual spaces.
key_points.evidence_quote: We are building the next frontier of AI, which is what we call spatial intelligence.

key_points.text: Digital simulations replace dangerous real-world data to teach robots safely and efficiently.
key_points.evidence_quote: We can replace all the data, all the evaluation we need in the real environments by using the data that can generate a scalable way in our digital world.

key_points.text: A consistent world model helps robots understand actions and environments better than simple video prediction.
key_points.evidence_quote: what we are building is a consistent word. Consistence both over space, over time, over different viewpoints and over different type of interactions.

key_points.text: Simulation allows robots to practice safely and learn faster than real-world testing alone.
key_points.evidence_quote: simulation essentially trying to predict how the environment is going to change when you apply the actions.

key_points.text: Simulation provides reliability by testing many different conditions like lighting and friction.
key_points.evidence_quote: you can do systematic randomizations and control and the variations of lighting, friction, geometries, object types, and also all different kinds of physical parameters to making sure you have sufficient coverage of the state space.

thesis: Fei-Fei Li and Yoon Joo Li argue that the next frontier of AI is spatial intelligence, which involves creating large world models to allow agents to perceive, reason with, and act within both physical and virtual spaces. They posit that solving robotics requires a new generation of AI built for three-dimensional reasoning to overcome data bottlenecks in training and evaluation by using a scalable digital-to-real pipeline.
